blocks.text: Group internal nodes by their height `d`, the maximum number of levels they can sift toward a leaf. At most `ceil(n / 2^(d+1))` nodes have height `d`, so, up to the harmless rounding term, aggregate repair is bounded by `n · Σ(d / 2^(d+1))` for `d >= 1`. This weighted geometric sum converges to a constant, giving `O(n)` bottom-up time. Repeated insertion instead has worst-case cost `Σ O(log i)` for heap sizes `i = 1..n`, which is `O(n log n)` and is attained when many inserted keys climb near the root. The methods establish the same heap invariant, but bottom-up construction exploits the fact that most nodes have very little possible travel.
